title: Social Media
goal: talk about online content, choose a response to contact, and explain a simple content idea.

study.title: What do you want to do with the post?

runs.text: To
follow
an account is to receive or find its updates through the platform. To
share
is to pass content on. A
comment
responds where other people can see it; a
DM
, or direct message, goes through a private messaging channel. Private here describes the channel, not a guarantee that the recipient will keep the information secret.

turns.speaker: Jules

runs.text: Did you see my photos from the street festival?

turns.en: Did you see my photos from the street festival?

turns.speaker: Carmen

runs.text: I saw the one with the dancers. Can you send me the other pictures?

turns.en: I saw the one with the dancers. Can you send me the other pictures?

turns.speaker: Jules

runs.text: Sure. I'll DM them to you.

turns.en: Sure. I'll DM them to you.

turns.speaker: Carmen

runs.text: Thanks. I'd rather not put the one with me on my profile.

turns.en: Thanks. I'd rather not put the one with me on my profile.

turns.speaker: Jules

runs.text: Okay. Do you want to choose a different one?

turns.en: Okay. Do you want to choose a different one?

turns.speaker: Carmen

runs.text: Yes, the picture of the food stands.

turns.en: Yes, the picture of the food stands.

blocks.caption: What do you want to do with the post? · Jules & Carmen

runs.text: “The photo came out great” praises the result. “Could you leave me out of the post?” sets a boundary. You can like the picture and still prefer not to be included. If you are planning to post a picture of someone, “Are you okay with me posting this?” lets them give a real answer.
A post
goes viral
when it spreads widely and quickly. There is no single number in this expression that guarantees it is viral.
Followers
follow an account;
likes
are reactions to a particular item.
Reach
describes how many people content gets to. These are different things: having many followers does not mean every follower sees or likes every post.

turns.speaker: Noah

runs.text: That dog video really took off.

turns.en: That dog video really took off.

turns.speaker: Tess

runs.text: I know. People keep sharing it.

turns.en: I know. People keep sharing it.

runs.text: Do you follow the account?

turns.speaker: Tess

runs.text: No, but I liked that one video.

turns.en: No, but I liked that one video.

blocks.caption: Reach, reaction, and interests · Noah & Tess

runs.text: “Took off” here means suddenly became popular. “I follow them for the recipes” explains a reason. “I'm not into their travel posts” expresses a preference without making it a rule for everyone.
Someone may criticize a post, tease a friend, or repeatedly provoke people.
Trolling
refers to deliberate provocation; a single disagreement does not prove that intention.

You can reply, ask a question, decline, or stop engaging. “What do you mean by that?” seeks clarification. “I don't agree, but I see your point” can continue a discussion. “Please stop messaging me” sets a direct boundary. “I'm going to block that account” describes a choice; blocking and reporting functions depend on the platform.
You do not have to keep answering to make the exchange polite. Equally, disagreement alone does not require ending it. Choose the action that serves your purpose.

turns.speaker: Owner

runs.text: What could we post about the new classes?

turns.en: What could we post about the new classes?

turns.speaker: Assistant

runs.text: A short video could show what happens in a class.

turns.en: A short video could show what happens in a class.

turns.speaker: Owner

runs.text: I don't want students on camera without asking them.

turns.en: I don't want students on camera without asking them.

turns.speaker: Assistant

runs.text: We could film you explaining an activity, then invite questions in the comments.

turns.en: We could film you explaining an activity, then invite questions in the comments.

turns.speaker: Owner

runs.text: Let's try that. What would the caption say?

turns.en: Let's try that. What would the caption say?

turns.speaker: Assistant

runs.text: “Curious about our Saturday art class? Here's a quick look at one activity. Message us if you'd like the schedule.”

turns.en: “Curious about our Saturday art class? Here's a quick look at one activity. Message us if you'd like the schedule.”

blocks.caption: A business content idea · Owner & Assistant

runs.text: This is a proposed communication plan, not a promise of audience growth. An
influencer
has an online audience they can influence; a
livestream
broadcasts as it happens; a
podcast
presents a series of episodes. Choose the format for the information you want to share.

Fictional facts: you liked a cooking clip and shared it with your sister. You do not follow its creator. Answer these partner questions: “Do you follow that account?” and “Why did you share the video?”
Possibility: “No, I just liked that clip. I shared it because my sister wants to learn that recipe.” Do not change the facts to make yourself a follower.
Partner: “Can I post this picture of us?” First, you agree but want them to ask before tagging your account. “Sure. Could you check with me before tagging me?” A
tag
links or identifies an account in a post.

Second, you do not want the picture posted. Say that clearly. “I'd rather you didn't post that one” or “Please don't post that picture” can both fit. Partner: “How about the landscape photo?” You are happy with that alternative; answer accordingly.

Fictional bookstore: staff can film a short book introduction or host a live question session. The manager wants a format people can watch later, and no one is available to answer live questions. Suggest the recorded introduction and explain why. Partner: “What should we ask people to do?” Suggest commenting with a book question or requesting the event schedule.
Solo route:

answer the supplied cues, then cover the study models and try the opposite picture preference. Write one usable caption for the bookstore. Check that your message, audience, and requested action are clear; neither agreement nor refusal is compulsory.

ja: 投稿を見る・共有する・反応する。
note: 見る、共有する、反応するは別の行動です。誘われても、共有しない選択を伝えられます。提案は結果の保証とは分けます。
